title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: election decree unknown a priori — elect cannot conclude they need not obey; no election-knowledge until they feel the study of obeying God
pass_a_gloss: Further, since the decree of election is unto men a priori plainly unknown, and not revealed unto the elect themselves except from effects and the testimony of the Spirit, it is not only false, but alien from reason and common sense, what the Arminians gather — that these elect can conclude with themselves that there is no need that they be solicitous concerning rendering obedience. For the elect themselves cannot have even the slenderest knowledge of their election, before they feel in themselves this study of obeying God, and of passing their life religiously: nor will the Spirit of God deign to exhibit this testimony unto a man wallowing in the mire of most foul lusts. How therefore will he conclude from the apprehension of his election that there is no need unto him of holiness of life, who otherwise cannot gather that he is elect, than from the effects of the Holy and sanctifying Spirit?
pass_b_english: Further: the election decree is plainly unknown to men a priori, and is revealed to the elect themselves only from effects and the Spirit's testimony. So what the Arminians gather — that these elect can conclude they need not be solicitous about rendering obedience — is not only false, but alien to reason and common sense. The elect themselves cannot have even the slenderest knowledge of their election before they feel in themselves this study of obeying God and living religiously. Nor will God's Spirit deign to give that testimony to a man wallowing in the mire of foulest lusts. How then will he conclude from apprehending his election that he needs no holiness of life — when he can gather he is elect no other way than from the effects of the Holy and sanctifying Spirit?
source_text: Porro, cum electionis decretum sit hominibus a priori plane incognitum, et non nisi ex effectis et Spiritus testimonio ipsis electis revelatum, non modo falsum, sed a ratione et sensu communi alienum est, quod colligunt Arminiani, posse hosce electos concludere apud se nil opus esse ut soliciti sint de praestanda obedientia. Nam ipsi electi ne tenuissimam quidem suae electionis cognitionem habere possunt, priusquam sentiant in se hoc studium obediendi Deo, et vitam suam religiose transigendi: neque Spiritus Dei dignabitur hoc testimonium homini in caeno libidinum turpissimarum volutanti exhibere. Quomodo igitur concludet ex apprehensione electionis suae nil sibi opus esse sanctitate vitae, qui aliter colligere non potest se esse electum, quam ex effectis Spiritus sancti et sanctificantis?
